chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jarud that he heard Abu Ja'far (AS) saying:

Regarding ila' (oath of abstention from conjugal relations), he is suspended after one year. I said, 'After one year?' He said, 'Yes, he is suspended after one year, so it does not contradict the earlier reports, because he said he is suspended after one year, and it is not in it that if it is less than that, he is not suspended. And this depends on the evidence of the context, and that may be set aside for another evidence, and we have previously presented what necessitates the return from it.'

key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Ila' (oath of abstention from conjugal relations)
key_terms.يُوقَفُ: He is suspended (legal status between full marriage and divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Ila' and how long does the suspension last according to Imam al-Baqir (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (AS) clarifies that the legal suspension (tawaqquf) in 'ila' occurs specifically after the completion of one year, reconciling this with other reports by noting that the absence of explicit text for the period before one year does not negate the ruling but relies on contextual inference (dalil al-khitab). This nuanced interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly method of harmonizing seemingly contradictory narrations through precise linguistic and legal analysis. The ruling emphasizes the preservation of the marital bond during the waiting period, distinguishing it from immediate divorce.
